entities.summary: Katrin Dagmar Göring-Eckardt is a German politician of the German Green Party. Starting her political activity in the now-former German Democratic Republic in the late 1980s, she has been a member of the German Bundestag since 1998. She became co-chair of her party caucus in the Bundestag (2002–2005) and the Greens' Vice President of the Bundestag on 18 October 2005, a position that she held until 2013 and would later reprise in 2021. In the November 2012 primary election, the Green Party chose her and Jürgen Trittin as the top two candidates for the Greens for the 2013 German federal election.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent figure in Germany's Green Party, Katrin Göring-Eckardt has played a key role in shaping environmental and social policies at the national level. Her tenure as Vice President of the Bundestag from 2005 to 2013 and again in 2021 highlights her influence on German politics.
